newsitem.title: UK: World coffee stocks seen falling in 1996/97 - Licht.
newsitem.headline: World coffee stocks seen falling in 1996/97 - Licht.

text.p: Ending world coffee stocks are expected to reach 35.4 million bags in the 1996/97 crop year, down from the 39.2 million reported for 1995/96, statistician F.O. Licht said in a repoort on Friday.
In its first estimate of the world balance for 1996/97, Licht said coffee stocks would fall to 34.7 percent of usage from a previous 41.2 percent.
Coffee stocks at the beginning of the crop year were forecast at 39.2 million bags after 46.3 million in 1995/96.
Licht said world coffee offtake was forecast at 98 million bags for 1996/97, suggesting a fairly balanced situation.
"This will prevent any replenishment of consumer stocks unless producers decide to unload stock onto the market."

Licht estimated total offtake in 1997/98 at 101.2 million bags, rising to 102.6 million bags the following year and 104.1 million bags in 1999/2000, assuming no increase in prices. But if prices were to rise annually by 10 percent, the outlook for world consumption would be significantly different, Licht said, forecasting 98.2 million bags for 1997/98, 97.6 million bags the next year and 97.0 million bags in 1999/2000.
"These predictions illustrate the danger of sponsoring measures aimed at increasing prices without due regard first being paid to the underlying market dynamics," it said.
